title: Right-pinched component comparison respects concrete corepresentable postcomposition
statement:
Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and path components of geometric realizations from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the concrete corepresented coherent functors of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Work in fixed universes large enough for all the following constructions. Let $C$ be a quasicategory small in the ambient universe, let $x,y,z$ be vertices, put $A=\mathfrak C[C]$, $P_t=\operatorname{Map}^R_C(x,t)$, and let $H_x:C\to\mathcal S$ be the specific functor with $H_x(t)=\operatorname{Sing}|A(x,t)|$ defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Write $p_{P_t}:|P_t|_Q\to P_t$ and $\theta_t:|P_t|_Q\to A(x,t)$ for the specified weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], and $u_t:A(x,t)\to\operatorname{Sing}|A(x,t)|$ for the characteristic-map unit of [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. Define the component bijection
$$\beta_t=\pi_0(u_t)\,\pi_0(\theta_t)\,\pi_0(p_{P_t})^{-1}:\pi_0P_t\longrightarrow\pi_0H_x(t).$$
For every edge $g:y\to z$ and every $a\in\pi_0P_y$, the postcomposition class of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] satisfies
$$\beta_z([g]a)=\pi_0(H_x(g))(\beta_y(a)).$$
Here $H_x(g)$ means the actual enriched postcomposition map associated to the image of $g$ under the displayed coherent functor. In particular, for every $2$-simplex of $C$ with edges $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to z$, and $w:x\to z$, one has
$$\beta_z([w])=\pi_0(H_x(g))(\beta_y([f])).$$
The assertions concern this specified comparison with the concrete singular-realization model, rather than an unspecified equivalent Hom functor. No compactness, filteredness, colimit, connectedness, or Kan condition on the simplicial sets $A(x,t)$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated compatibility extracted from the returned compact-stage proof, step 5: HTT Section 2.2.4, Proposition 2.2.4.1 (pinched-to-rigidification comparison), together with the Section 5.1.3 opening construction of the concrete corepresentable functor. The subset inclusion {0,2} into {0,1,2} in Definition 1.1.5.1 supplies the triangle compatibility. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical comparison; online source retrieval returned HTTP 429 in this repair and an archive remains WANTED.

proof.text: For an edge $v:x\to t$, let $\widetilde v\in A(x,t)_0$ be the image of the vertex $\{0,1\}$ in the simplex-colimit construction of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], and put $m_v=u_t(\widetilde v)$. By [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution], $p_{P_t}$ and $\theta_t$ are weak homotopy equivalences and $Q^0=\Delta^0$; the copy of $Q^0$ indexed by $v$ maps respectively to the vertex $v$ of $P_t$ and to $\widetilde v$ of $A(x,t)$. Thus $\pi_0(\theta_t)\pi_0(p_{P_t})^{-1}([v])=[\widetilde v]$. By [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak], $\pi_0(u_t)$ is a bijection and $m_v$ is the singular vertex of $|\widetilde v|$. Weak equivalences induce component bijections by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so the specified $\beta_t$ is a bijection and $\beta_t([v])=[m_v]$. This computes the specified inverse on components without choosing a simplicial inverse.

source.place: Section 2.2.4 opening and Proposition 2.2.4.1, printed p.88; degree-zero formula from the cited pinched-resolution statement; Section 5.1.3 opening, printed pp.319-320. Agent expansion of the component formula.

proof.text: Let $\sigma:\Delta^2\to C$ have the edges $f:x\to y$, $g:y\to z$, $w:x\to z$. By the defining simplex colimit in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], it gives an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^2]\to A$. Its $(0,2)$ mapping set is the nerve of the two-element inclusion poset $\{0,2\}\subset\{0,1,2\}$. The first vertex is the image of the $02$ edge. The second is the union of $\{0,1\}$ and $\{1,2\}$, hence the composite of their vertices. Compatibility of the colimit cocone with the three face inclusions identifies their images with $\widetilde w$ and $\widetilde g\circ\widetilde f$, respectively. The displayed inclusion therefore gives an actual simplicial edge $e$ in $A(x,z)$ from $\widetilde w$ to $\widetilde g\circ\widetilde f$. This argument also applies when vertices or edges of $\sigma$ are degenerate.

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.1 and Remark 1.1.5.2, printed pp.20-21; Definitions 1.1.5.3-1.1.5.5 and the simplex-colimit construction, printed pp.21-23. Direct two-subset computation.

proof.text: The map $u_z$ sends $e$ to an edge of $H_x(z)$, whose endpoints are $m_w$ and $u_z(\widetilde g\circ\widetilde f)$. Its realization is a path between those vertices by the quotient realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The unit is an enriched functor $A\to A^{\mathrm{top}}$ by [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], so $u_z(\widetilde g\circ\widetilde f)=u_{y,z}(\widetilde g)\circ u_y(\widetilde f)$, where $u_{y,z}$ is the same characteristic-map unit on $A(y,z)$. In that definition the coherent functor sends $g$ to precisely postcomposition by $u_{y,z}(\widetilde g)$: the adjunction unit on the $g$ simplex is its defining map into the colimit. Consequently the second endpoint is the actual vertex $H_x(g)(m_f)$. Taking path components and using step 1 gives $\beta_z([w])=[m_w]=[H_x(g)(m_f)]=\pi_0(H_x(g))(\beta_y([f]))$, proving the asserted triangle clause.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1-1.1.5.5, printed pp.20-22, and Section 5.1.3 opening, printed pp.319-320. Agent expansion using the enriched-unit and concrete-action formulas explicitly stated in the cited definition.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $a\in\pi_0P_y$, the edge-representation clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives an edge $f:x\to y$ with $[f]=a$. The edges $f,g$ define a map $\Lambda^2_1\to C$, because they agree at $y$. Fill it by the quasicategory condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and call its $02$ edge $w$. The triangle clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives $[g]a=[g][f]=[w]$. Step 3 now yields $\beta_z([g]a)=\beta_z([w])=\pi_0(H_x(g))(\beta_y(a))$. If $\pi_0P_y$ is empty this assertion is vacuous. Only the inner horn in $C$ was filled; no Kan hypothesis on $A(x,t)$ was used.
